title: The Butler
why: Stages the Greensboro Woolworth's lunch-counter sit-in that began on 1 February 1960, intercut with the White House it changed.

title: Groundhog Day
why: The date, over and over. Punxsutawney, 2 February.

title: La Bamba
why: The Day the Music Died — Buddy Holly, Ritchie Valens and the Big Bopper killed in the Clear Lake crash, 3 February 1959.
alt: The Buddy Holly Story (1978); Serpico (shot 3 February 1971)

title: Patty Hearst
why: Schrader opens with the SLA kidnapping Hearst from her Berkeley apartment on 4 February 1974.
alt: Facebook founded, 4 Feb 2004 — The Social Network

title: United
why: The Munich air disaster of 6 February 1958 and what was left of Busby's team afterwards.

title: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
why: The first chapter opens on a title card: Saturday, February 8th, 1969. Two-thirds of the film is that one day.
alt: East of Eden (John Steinbeck's Feb 8 setting)

title: The Beatles: Eight Days a Week
why: The Ed Sullivan Show broadcast of 9 February 1964 — 73 million viewers, the hinge of the touring years.

title: Bridge of Spies
why: The whole film is a negotiation for one morning: the Abel/Powers exchange on the Glienicke Bridge, 10 February 1962.

title: Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
why: Ends on the walk out of Victor Verster Prison, 11 February 1990.
alt: Invictus (2009), which opens on the same footage

title: Creation
why: Darwin was born on 12 February 1809 (as was Lincoln); the film is his struggle to publish.

title: Slaughterhouse-Five
why: Billy Pilgrim comes unstuck in time around the firebombing of Dresden on the night of 13/14 February 1945.

title: The St. Valentine's Day Massacre
why: Seven of Bugs Moran's men shot against a garage wall on North Clark Street, 14 February 1929.
alt: Sleepless in Seattle (Empire State Building, Valentine's Day); Raging Bull (LaMotta–Robinson, 14 Feb 1951); Valentine's Day (2010)

title: Sophie Scholl: The Final Days
why: Covers 18–22 February 1943 hour by hour, from the leaflet drop at Munich University on the 18th to the guillotine.

title: Letters from Iwo Jima
why: The American landings on Iwo Jima, 19 February 1945, seen from inside the Japanese tunnels.

title: Hidden Figures
why: Built to one launch: John Glenn's three orbits aboard Friendship 7, 20 February 1962 — 'get the girl to check the numbers'.

title: Malcolm X
why: The film is framed by the Audubon Ballroom assassination of 21 February 1965.

title: Miracle
why: USA 4, USSR 3 at Lake Placid, 22 February 1980. Do you believe in miracles?
alt: Sophie Scholl executed, 22 Feb 1943; Washington's birthday

title: Flags of Our Fathers
why: The second flag-raising on Mount Suribachi, 23 February 1945, and the photograph that ate six lives.

title: 20 Days in Mariupol
why: Mstyslav Chernov's footage starts on 24 February 2022, the first morning of the full-scale invasion, and counts the days.

title: One Night in Miami...
why: Entirely set on the evening of 25 February 1964, in a Hampton House motel room, after Cassius Clay beat Sonny Liston.
alt: Ali (2001), which opens with the same fight

title: Cool Runnings
why: The Jamaican four-man bobsleigh crash at Calgary, 27 February 1988 — the run the film ends on.

title: Waco: The Rules of Engagement
why: The ATF raid on Mount Carmel that began the 51-day siege, 28 February 1993.
alt: The assassination of Olof Palme, 28 Feb 1986

title: Leap Year
why: The entire premise: Anna races to Dublin to propose on 29 February, the one day tradition allows it.
alt: The Pirates of Penzance (1983) — Frederic, born on the 29th, is 'a little boy of five'
